Matched RecHarness Amazon task: four datasets Movies_and_TV,
Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from the corrected family-specific cold start supplied by the host. Preserve that model family. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.

METHOD: self_evolverec
COMPARISON MODEL FAMILY: bert4rec. Start from the supplied corrected baseline; keep its backbone family throughout search, including initial proposals, merging and debugging. Do not fall back to SASRec or another model family. Keep seed 42, maximum epochs 200, batches per epoch 200 and the supplied splits/evaluator fixed. All models use LEFT-padded histories: the readout must use the final nonpadding position, never count-1. BERT4Rec uses a reserved mask token with masked-target training and appended-mask inference; do not expose a shifted prediction target through bidirectional input. Preserve checkpoint and embedded predictor consistency. Diagnosis uses family-specific sample_batch and ModelView; keep log2feats(sequence), item_emb and predict_score(features, items) compatible. One trained model/checkpoint per category; no independent score fusion.

MANDATORY SINGLE-MODEL EXPERIMENT: train one independent model per category.
Do not implement ensembles, bagging, boosting of independent predictors, stacking,
multi-seed/checkpoint averaging, score/rank voting, mixtures of independently fitted
experts, or neural scores combined with separately fitted transition/popularity scores.
Each category must load exactly one independently trained model/checkpoint at prediction.
Jointly trained internal layers/features of one network are allowed. Four category
models are necessary for routing and do not constitute an ensemble. All hypotheses,
code generation, debugging, reviews and memory use must respect this constraint even
if an upstream generic prompt suggests an ensemble. The host audits the actual
predictor before accepting validation scores; violations fail the trial and consume
their training budget. Do not read other trials or reuse their trained checkpoints.


Diagnostic task adapter: diagnosis_tools.py must retain class DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
and method run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions.
It must also retain callable diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning
the diagnostic interpretation prompt using measured metrics and their definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
family-specific sequential-model compatibility contract; preserve the host ModelView interfaces and adapt probes to that family. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.
Only public interaction histories, item titles, descriptions and timestamps are available.
Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

NATIVE ROLE: Writing Agent
You are a senior researcher responsible for proposing new ideas to address a defined research problem. You will receive:
-The research problem, including its qualitative user diagnosis feedback, code analysis of models and diagnosis tool, and available data.
- A starting research idea, possibly with its evolution history
- Inspirations from earlier attempts
- A list of related online search results
- A research progress score (0-100%) indicating how far the idea has advanced

Your goal is to identify future research directions that address the target problem, using the starting point, prior attempts, and related works. You should analyze existing methods, identify connections, and propose practical algorithms that can be implemented with the available data.

Follow this structure to think and write:

1. **Extract insights**  
   Identify 3-5 scientific insights from the starting point and 3-5 from related works. For each insight, explain in 2-3 sentences how it relates to the target problem.

2. **Organize research directions**  
   Group the insights into 3-5 coherent directions (for example, persona/trait design, feedback schema, better behavioral rules, or model classes).

3. **Build a structured framework**  
   Create a conceptual map (such as a taxonomy, grid, or matrix) that unifies existing methods, reveals patterns, and highlights gaps.

4. **Generate and evaluate ideas**  
   - First, propose 3-10 algorithmic ideas of varying originality and complexity. Each idea should be:
     - As simple, minimal, and atomic as possible but not trivial  
     - Include brief pseudocode or logical steps where helpful.  
     - Include references to the related works.
   - For each idea, critically assess as a senior researcher with one positive and one negative reason:
     - Originality (0-10): Is the idea new? Is the idea a novel combination of well-known techniques? Is it clearly different from previous contributions?
     - Future Potential (0-10): Will others build on these ideas? Does this idea solve a hard problem more effectively than prior work? Does it point to a new research direction?
     - Code Difficulty (0-10): How complex is the implementation? How much code is required? How much time is required to implement?
   - Then, select the single best idea from that list for detailed reporting, based on the research progress score:
     - If progress is relatively early, prioritize feasible, easy-to-implement ideas with long-term promise.
     - If progress is relatively mature, prioritize seminal ideas with high-impacts for the next-generation research
     - Otherwise, balance ambition and implementation feasibility

5. **Write the report in Markdown**  
   For the selected idea, include:
   - A synthesis of insights and proposed directions  
   - The structured framework of existing methods and the new algorithm  
   - A list of new ideas with their assessment scores
   - Detailed description of the chosen/best idea, including rationale, pseudocode, and implementation notes

The report must be focused, technically accurate. Being concise with 200-500 words without trivial and redundant information.
Support all claims with evidence and references, and remain tightly aligned with the target problem.

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The probe expects BERT4Rec: scaled item embeddings plus absolute position embeddings, dropout, a bidirectional Transformer with PAD keys masked, and final normalization. PAD=0; MASK=itemnum+1. Serving retains the latest maxlen−1 interactions and appends MASK. Its final-slot feature represents the sequence for scoring; no count−1 readout is used.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` accesses the actual network through `view.model`, alongside `item_emb`, `log2feats(sequence)`, `predict_score(features, items)`, training histories, and dataset routing. The loader supplies `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` with B×L tensors. `run_full_diagnosis` runs in evaluation mode without gradients, then restores model mode and random-generator states.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Embedding alignment:** Maps mean pairwise cosine among up to 2,048 seeded real-item embeddings to [0,1], excluding PAD/MASK. Higher values indicate alignment; 0.5 means approximately zero mean cosine, not demonstrated representation quality.
- **Sampler and margins:** Checks reserved tokens, tensor shapes, real target IDs, and MASK replacement at every supervised position. Across at most ten batches, reports positive-minus-negative mean, tenth percentile, negative-win rate, and margins below 0.5. Larger margins and fewer negative wins indicate stronger in-sample pair separation.
- **Serving parity:** Reloads the exported category checkpoint and requires exact state-tensor identity. Compares explicit encoder, ModelView, internal scoring, exported prediction, and batched versus individual results. Passing requires finite, tolerance-matched scores, identical rankings, and short/full/truncated/batched coverage.

# Perturbation & Tests

Sensitivity runs only after sampler and parity checks pass. Up to 64 seeded training users contribute one eligible prefix endpoint, with a previously unseen target and 99 unique prefix-excluded negatives.

Paired variants delete equally many recent or older visible items into PAD holes, preserving positions, or swap the last two items. Fixed candidates support target-score/rank, reciprocal-rank, hit@10 changes, top-10 overlap, and ranking agreement. These reveal history sensitivity; greater sensitivity is not inherently better. Summaries include 500 paired-user bootstrap intervals.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

Returns `metrics` and `metric_definitions`: status, embedding/margin measurements, sampler checks, prefix counts, parity, gated sensitivity, and elapsed time. Sensitivity includes per-category summaries and individual outcomes; four-category macro results remain unavailable.

Null means unavailable. These are training-prefix diagnostics, not host validation quality. They cannot establish sampler provenance, uniform training negatives, seed robustness, external-label invariance, unavailable metadata, or simulator traits.


 ## Search results
The strongest methodological matches are [Zhang & Nanda, ICLR 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16042) and [Heimersheim & Nanda, 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.15255). Activation patching replaces selected internal activations with those from a controlled alternative input, locating components responsible for a specified behavioral difference. Both emphasize that corruption choice, metric, and patch direction affect conclusions. Clean-to-corrupted restoration and corrupted-to-clean disruption provide complementary evidence; neither alone establishes a complete or unique mechanism.

Direct sequential-recommendation evidence includes a [September 2026 temporal-attribution benchmark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.27201), covering BERT4Rec. It reports stronger faithfulness for Integrated Gradients/GradientSHAP than raw attention, with gradient-weighted attention less reliable on long histories. Its evaluation uses a separately trained masking-robust probe, so that protocol does not directly satisfy the requested frozen-checkpoint constraint. [Liu et al., 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.07898) demonstrate component-level activation patching for relevance judgments in LLMs, offering methodological precedent rather than BERT4Rec-specific evidence.

Proposed adaptation, inferred from these methods: use one frozen BERT4Rec checkpoint and separately intervene on item embeddings, item order, and positional embeddings. Replace identities while holding positions fixed; permute the same item multiset; change position IDs while preserving identities, order, padding masks, and appended-mask readout. Patch residual streams first, then attention-head/MLP outputs, measuring fixed-candidate score-margin changes and restoration. Compare against identity patches, random components of matched size, and random interventions matched for position and item frequency. Position-ID interventions may be out of distribution. Report effects across users and controls as evidence about model computation; recommendation quality remains a separate validation HR@10 measurement.

---

Recent evidence supports testing diagnostic correctness separately from recommendation accuracy. A [2024 metamorphic-testing study](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.infsof.2024.107410) exposed reliability problems across LibRec, PREA, and Surprise using input transformations with expected output relationships. This supports controlled checks, but does not establish that diagnostic-driven training changes improve BERT4Rec. Proposed task-specific controls: inject incorrect left-padding readout, target leakage, or mask-token misuse into isolated diagnostic fixtures; verify detection and recovery after correction. Include unchanged-model controls to measure false alarms. These are proposed experiments, not published findings for this benchmark.

Sampled ranking and full-catalog behavior require separate interpretation. [RecSys 2025 research](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) evaluates sampling through fidelity, separability, exposure robustness, and predictive power. Earlier [sampled-metric analysis](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) demonstrates that sampling can reverse model comparisons even in expectation. Therefore, training-prefix reconstruction measures fit; pinned 99-negative validation HR@10 measures the host objective; full-catalog unseen-item recommendations describe another ranking setting. Improvements in one do not establish improvements in the others.

For uncertainty, compare baseline and candidate on identical validation users and candidates. Proposed analysis: bootstrap paired per-user hit differences within each category, then average the four category differences equally; report the macro gain and 95% interval. [Search/recommendation significance research](https://piret.info/pubs/2023/SIGIR23-InferenceAtScale) supports bootstrap/randomization approaches and emphasizes effect size. Such intervals condition on the fixed users/candidates and trained models; they do not capture training-seed variation or remove adaptive-search optimism. Judge diagnostic usefulness by whether prespecified repairs improve unchanged host validation HR@10, using no test labels or additional fitted predictors.

---

Recent work supports separating recommendation relevance from redundancy, functional complementarity and verified compatibility. [Function-based labels for complementary recommendation (2025)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167865525003976) introduces explicit functional labels and 2,759 human-annotated item pairs, helping distinguish complementary use from broad similarity. Suggested adaptation for this task: annotate each recommendation with evidence from histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps; distinguish duplicate function from a distinct supported use; require explicit specifications for compatibility claims. For conjunctive requirements, mark each condition supported, contradicted or unknown; abstain from an overall compatibility judgment when a required condition is unknown. These are proposed probes, not validated metrics. Historical interaction alone cannot establish current intent or satisfaction.

Human agreement must be checked locally. [From IR to RecSys (2025; revised 2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.23312) finds richer metadata and longer histories improve agreement, but item-level agreement remains moderate despite strong aggregate system-ranking agreement. [Can LLM be a Personalized Judge? (2024)](https://aclanthology.org/2024.findings-emnlp.592/) reports weak overall alignment with personal preferences and better agreement on high-certainty cases; third-party annotators also struggle to infer individual preferences. Practical implication: double-annotate a sample across all four categories, separate factual evidence judgments from personal utility judgments, and compare automated labels against adjudicated human labels. Report agreement, disagreement examples and abstention coverage by criterion. Use actual user feedback only when observed; mark missing feedback explicitly. Keep these diagnostics supplementary to the pinned macro validation HR@10."}]
